titles.130: J.X open: Variata defense was not for Reformed favor — Invariata equally dear; Leipzig Colloquy; Museus/Chemnitz on fuller Variata
titles.131: J.X: Partly for Philippica fame — Reformed hold Melanchthon's name with Luther's; do not sneer at anti-idolatry Reformers as heretics
titles.132: J.X: Partly for any Augsburg Confession — so Pontificii cannot brand alteration and strip Protestants of Religious Peace
titles.133: J.X: Partly for Invariata-only party — do not cling to early wording into papal species-presence sense; Naumburg 1561 preface warned
titles.134: J.X: Or if they leave that sense for an obscurer one unknown to Pontificii — Jesuit-like equivocation charge (Dorsche p.183)
titles.135: J.X: Besides — so Hoffmann of Helmstedt and other Lutherans cannot press that the Formula Concord inserted a spurious AC exemplar
titles.136: J.X close: Above all for Truth and Protestant peace — both sides agree on Lord's Supper substance; do not devour each other over words while Rome dances

latin.130:
J. X.
Quae hactenus pro Variata seu Philippica Confessione Augustana disputavimus, non in Reformatorum gratiam disputata fuisse quivis facile intelligat, utpote quibus Invariata Confessio non minus grata, atque Variata est, id quod vel ex solo Colloquio Lipsiaco, superiori seculo Saxonicos inter, Brandenb. & Hassiacos Theologos, habito, satis superque constat, nisi quod cum Joh. Museo ex Martino Chemnitio, de posteriori teneant, plerosque Articulos in ea fusius deductos & uberius declaratos esse, multa etiam utilia in ista editione reperiri.
latin.131: Disputata interim sunt partim in gratiam Philippicae famae, quam perinde atque Lutheri, in deliciis habent Reformati, omnibus Reformatoribus Pontificiae Idolomaniae hanc gratiam deberi augurati, ne Scripta Factaque istorum vel temere suggillentur, vel exagitentur odiose haereseosque coarguantur;
latin.132: Partim in gratiam Augustanae Confessionis cujuscunque, ne a Pontificiis [quod ut saepe factum, ita hodieque fit] alterationis hujusmodi infimuletur, ob quam Protestantes Pace Religiosa indigni ab Imperatore Augusto aliisque Statibusque Imperii Pontificiis, censeri debeant;
latin.133: Partim in gratiam Invariatae Confessionis in specie, hancque solam & cum oppressione ac exterminio Variatae, amplectentium, ne, dum nimis superstitiose verbis prioris inhaerere satagunt, ad phrasin Pontificiam de praesentia Corporis & Sanguinis Christi in Coena sub Speciebus panis & vini, hujusque phraseos sensum, eo tempore, quo Confessio edebatur, Occidentali Ecclesiae unice receptum, adigantur, id quod metuendum fuisse jam olim innuere Status Imperii, Naunburgi Anno 61. congregati, in praefatione sua, Augustanae Confessioni Invariatae praemissa & Ferdinando Imperatori inscripta;
latin.134: Vel dum ab hoc sensu recedunt, & obscuriorem, certe Pontificiis Doctoribus & Statibus Imperii plerisque isto tempore ignotum, sequuntur, a Dorscheo cit. loc. pag. 183. in fine traditum, aequivocationis, Jesuiticis haud absimilis, rei inveniantur, ab illis alias haud raro, etsi satis perperam, Reformatis impingi solitae.
latin.135: Praeterea, ne ab Hoffmanno Helmstadiensi aliisque Lutheranis Theologis, jure urgeantur, Formulae Concordiae spurium Augustanae Confessionis Exemplar insertum esse; vide Hoffmanni Apologiam ad D. Olearium & Paulum Nicandrum, pag. 691. citatam Auctori des Anhangs der ausführlichen Behauptung pag. 29. & feqq.
latin.136: Partim denique & maxime omnium in gratiam & Veritatis & Pacis Protestanticae, ne, quemadmodum Evangelicorum utraque pars in re & substantia Veritatis, quoad Articulum de Sacra Coena, consentit, (id quod infra ad oculum patebit) ita litigiis de verbis, in alterutra Confessione Augustana repertis, distrahantur & inter tripudia Pontificia mordeant se mutuo, a se mutuo consumendi.

pass_a.130: J. X. What we have disputed thus far for the Variata or Philippica Augsburg Confession, anyone easily understands was not disputed for the favor of the Reformed, seeing that to them the Invariata Confession is no less welcome than the Variata is, which is established more than enough even from the Leipzig Colloquy alone held in the last century among the Saxon, Brandenburg, and Hessian theologians, except that with John Museus from Martin Chemnitz they hold concerning the later one that most articles in it are drawn out more fully and declared more richly, and that many useful things also are found in that edition.
pass_a.131: Meanwhile they have been disputed partly for the favor of Philippica fame, which the Reformed hold in delight equally with Luther's, judging that this favor is owed to all the Reformers of pontifical idol-madness, lest the writings and deeds of those men be either rashly sneered at, or odiously harassed and convicted of heresy;
pass_a.132: Partly for the favor of the Augsburg Confession of whichever form, lest it be charged by the Pontificii [which as it has often been done, so it is done even today] with an alteration of this kind, on account of which Protestants ought to be judged unworthy of the Religious Peace by the Emperor Augustus and the other pontifical Estates of the Empire;
pass_a.133: Partly for the favor of the Invariata Confession in particular, and of those who embrace this alone and with the oppression and extermination of the Variata, lest, while they strive too superstitiously to cling to the words of the earlier one, they be driven to the pontifical phrase concerning the presence of the Body and Blood of Christ in the Supper under the species of bread and wine, and to the sense of this phrase uniquely received in the Western Church at the time when the Confession was published — which the Estates of the Empire gathered at Naumburg in the year 61 already long ago hinted was to be feared, in their preface prefixed to the Invariata Augsburg Confession and addressed to Emperor Ferdinand;
pass_a.134: Or while they withdraw from this sense and follow an obscurer one, certainly unknown to most pontifical doctors and Estates of the Empire at that time — handed down by Dorsche at the cited place page 183 at the end — they are found guilty of a matter of equivocation not unlike Jesuit ones, which those men elsewhere not rarely, though quite wrongly, are accustomed to pin on the Reformed.
pass_a.135: Besides, lest they be rightly pressed by Hoffmann of Helmstedt and other Lutheran theologians that a spurious exemplar of the Augsburg Confession was inserted into the Formula of Concord; see Hoffmann's Apology to Doctor Olearius and Paul Nicander, page 691, cited by the Author of the Appendix of the Ausführliche Behauptung, pages 29 and following.
pass_a.136: Partly finally and most of all for the favor both of Truth and of Protestant Peace, lest, just as either part of the Evangelicals agrees in the matter and substance of the Truth as to the Article on the Holy Supper (which will be clear to the eye below), so they be pulled apart by quarrels about words found in either Augsburg Confession and amid pontifical dances bite one another, to be consumed by one another.

130: J. X. Anyone can see that what we have argued so far for the Variata or Philippica Augsburg Confession was not argued to favor the Reformed.
To them the Invariata is no less welcome than the Variata — clear enough from the Leipzig Colloquy alone in the last century among Saxon, Brandenburg, and Hessian theologians.
With John Museus, following Martin Chemnitz, they only add that in the later edition most articles are drawn out more fully and stated more richly, and that many useful things appear there.
131: Meantime the case was argued partly for Philippica fame, which the Reformed cherish as they do Luther's.
They reckon that favor owed to every Reformer who broke with papal idol-madness: do not rashly sneer at their writings and deeds, nor bait them as heretics.
132: Partly it was for the Augsburg Confession in either form: so the papal side — as they often have, and still do — cannot charge this kind of alteration, and then say Protestants deserve to lose the Religious Peace before the Emperor and the other papal Estates of the Empire.
133: Partly it was for the Invariata in particular — and for those who hug that form alone while crushing and wiping out the Variata.

If they cling too superstitiously to the earlier wording, they can be pushed into the papal phrase about Christ's Body and Blood present in the Supper under the species of bread and wine, in the sense the Western Church alone then held when the Confession was issued.
The Imperial Estates at Naumburg in 1561 already flagged that danger in the preface they set before the Invariata and addressed to Emperor Ferdinand.
134: Or when they leave that sense and take an obscurer one — one most papal doctors and Imperial Estates then did not know — Dorsche at the place cited (p. 183, end) still leaves them open to a charge of equivocation not unlike Jesuit practice.
Papal writers elsewhere often pin that charge on the Reformed, though quite wrongly.
135: Besides, so Hoffmann of Helmstedt and other Lutheran theologians cannot rightly press that the Formula of Concord slipped in a spurious Augsburg Confession exemplar.
See Hoffmann's Apology to Dr. Olearius and Paul Nicander (p. 691), cited by the author of the Appendix to the Ausführliche Behauptung (pp. 29ff.).
136: Finally — and most of all — it was for Truth and for Protestant peace.
Both Evangelical sides already agree in the matter and substance of the truth on the article of the Lord's Supper (that will be plain below).
They must not be torn apart by fights over words in either Augsburg Confession, and bite one another to pieces while Rome dances.
